Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "The access list for North Window Studio is kept in a blue binder beside the entrance, with a matching copy in the building manager’s office. It covers the print room, the small recording booth, and the shared worktable, but not the locked cabinet used by the ceramics group. The binder is updated when a member joins, changes their usual hours, or returns a key. Mara Chen maintains it for the studio cooperative, while building manager Luis Ortega handles requests involving the outer door. Both copies show the date of the latest revision on the inside cover.

At the monthly meeting on 14 March, members agreed to keep the list organized by room rather than by surname. That makes it easier to check who can enter a particular space without passing around everyone’s contact details. Each entry includes a member’s name, the room or rooms they may use, and any hours that differ from the regular schedule. Phone numbers remain on a separate emergency sheet in the manager’s office. A person’s access is not changed just because they stop attending meetings; Mara asks them directly whether they still need it.

The entrance sheet has a short note explaining that a listed name does not unlock every door. The outer entrance uses a fob, and individual rooms may have separate keys or codes. “I can let you into the building, but I can’t promise the print room is ready,” Luis said when a new member asked about evening access. His distinction has helped prevent confusion during events, when visitors sometimes assume the shared entrance fob also opens equipment rooms. Members are asked not to lend their fobs, even to another cooperative member, because the entry log records the assigned holder.

1. **Room entries.** Mara checks the room sections against the signed access forms before adding a name. The print room has a posted closing time of 9 p.m., while the recording booth can be reserved later by members who have completed its orientation. The worktable has no separate key, but evening use still depends on having access to the outer entrance. A note beside each section identifies the person to contact about a missing key or a room-specific code. The list does not include reservation times, which are kept on the shared calendar.

2. **Temporary access.** A visiting artist may receive a temporary entry fob for a workshop or installation, but the sponsoring member must submit the dates and rooms in advance. Luis records the fob number and return date in the manager’s log; Mara adds the visitor’s name to a dated insert rather than the permanent binder. If an event runs late, the sponsor contacts Luis instead of changing the posted end time by hand. This process applies to invited guests as well as paid workshop instructors, although instructors may also receive a separate equipment orientation from the relevant room lead.

The group reviewed two discrepancies at the March meeting. A print-room key had been returned to the labeled envelope, but its return had not been marked in the binder. In a separate case, a member’s entry fob worked at the outer door but did not appear in the building’s current assignment list. Neither issue required changing another person’s room access. Mara corrected the paper record after checking the envelope, and Luis asked the building office to compare the fob number with its electronic register. Until that comparison was complete, the member could use the entrance during staffed hours.

There is no shared spreadsheet containing the full access list. A password-protected file held by Mara contains the same room entries as the binder, so she can prepare a fresh printout if the blue copy is damaged. She stores the file on the cooperative’s restricted drive and does not send it through the general mailing list. Members can ask to check their own entry in person, and corrections are made after Mara confirms the relevant form or speaks with the room lead. The separate emergency sheet is reviewed each season, since phone numbers are more likely to change than room permissions.

When a member leaves the cooperative, the departure form includes a space for any fob or key that must be returned. The room lead checks shared equipment, and Luis removes the person’s outer-door permission after the agreed end date. Mara then removes the name from the active binder and files the old form with the cooperative’s records. If a key is still missing, the relevant room lead decides whether the lock needs attention; the access-list process does not automatically treat every late return as a security incident. Any replacement key is numbered and recorded before it is handed out.

The next review is scheduled for 11 June, before the summer workshop program begins. Mara will bring the current binder and the forms received since March, and Luis will bring a report of active fobs without member contact details. The room leads will check closing hours and orientation requirements, especially for the recording booth, which has gained new equipment. The cooperative has not decided whether to move the binder to a wall-mounted holder, since members use the entrance area for deliveries and there is limited space.
